title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only work at the document level (or on narrow, task-specific token tasks such as spell checking), so they cannot localize which tokens in a text are anomalous. The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, releases three token-annotated benchmarks (SMS_Spam with injected character corruption, Restaurant Review semantic anomalies, Grammar errors), and proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal word-level token embeddings (BERT-base-uncased embeddings aggregated by element-wise max pooling over subwords) and scores each test token by its nearest-neighbor distance, aggregating token scores by mean for document-level scores. TokenCore achieves the best average token-level AUROC (0.7145) and document-level AUROC (0.7335) among 7 methods, ranking first at token level on Review (0.8271) and Grammar (0.6371) and at document level on Review (0.9594), while ECOD/iForest remain better on the character-corruption SMS_Spam token-level task.

text: Cloning into 'repo'...

why: The authors released the method code (TokenCore.py: memory bank + nearest-neighbor token scoring), the alignment/annotation utilities (align.py, tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py) and all three annotated datasets locally in data/ (grammar .npy/.json, restaurant_review, sms_spam), so the core logic can be kept verbatim. What is NOT released is a runnable entrypoint: the only end-to-end artifact is Demo.ipynb (with frozen outputs), there is no requirements.txt, and TokenCore.py consumes precomputed token-embedding matrices, so the BERT-base-uncased embedding extraction, the 50/50 split and the token-level AUROC computation have to be rebuilt as a script from the notebook before the target number for Grammar (C1) can be produced. Keep authors' logic, rebuild the missing driver.
est_runtime: ~25-35 min wall clock on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM: ~10 min installing torch (CPU wheel), transformers, scikit-learn; ~1 min BERT-base download; ~1-3 min BERT forward pass over 300 short Grammar documents; seconds for the max-pooling, memory-bank build and brute-force nearest-neighbor scoring; plus the driver-script rewrite from the notebook and one clean end-to-end re-run.
blockers: no dependency file: torch/transformers/sklearn/numpy must be pinned by hand (works on Python 3.12)
TokenCore.py takes embedding matrices only; the BERT max-pooling-over-subwords front-end exists only inside the notebook, so the pipeline must be extracted into a script
Demo.ipynb is 3.8 MB of stored outputs; it must be rewritten/cleared before execution
no GPU on this machine (BERT-base CPU inference only, which is acceptable at this scale)

Grammar token-level AUROC is computed over very few anomalous tokens (~15 anomalous docs in the test half), and the split is random, so the absolute value 0.6371 will depend on the split seed and may drift

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction of claim C1: TokenCore's token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (0.6371, tolerance ±0.02 absolute). We clone the authors' repo, keep TokenCore.py/align.py/json_to_npy.py verbatim, and rebuild only the missing driver that Demo.ipynb used to hide: read the released grammar annotations (data/grammar_correction_labeled.json and data/grammar.npy), build the 300-document corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10), take 50% of the normal documents as the memory-bank training set (R6, A8), run BERT-base-uncased over the remaining normal + anomalous documents, max-pool subword embeddings into word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1, R2/R9, A3/A4), fit the authors' TextCore memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3, A2), score every test token by Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4, A1/A9), and compute pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC plus the mean-aggregated document-level scores (Eq. 3, R5, A5). The paper value is a single split-free number, so the only real drift risk is split randomness on 300 short documents; we therefore report a primary seeded run plus a small multi-seed spread so the ±0.02 band can be interpreted. Only the Grammar dataset is needed for C1, but the same driver is written so that running it on restaurant_review / sms_spam later costs nothing extra.
steps: Clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git into ./TokenCore and record the commit hash; do not modify TokenCore.py, align.py or tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py.

Create a venv/conda env on Python 3.12 and pip install torch (CPU wheel from the default index), transformers, numpy, scikit-learn, tqdm, requests; write the resolved versions into requirements.txt (the file the README references but the repo lacks).

Run src/inspect_data.py: dump shapes/dtypes/keys of data/grammar.npy and the JSON schema of data/grammar_correction_labeled.json, and print the actual class/function signatures of TokenCore.py and align.py. Decide the exact field names for words, token labels and document labels, and confirm the .npy is a token/label array rather than precomputed embeddings (43 KB is far too small for 300x768 floats).

Implement src/data_grammar.py against the inspected schema; load all 300 Grammar documents and hard-assert 300 documents / 270 normal / 30 anomalous (10% rate, R10) and consistency of the document labels with the token labels (R11).

Implement the split: with seed 0, shuffle the 270 normal documents, take the first 135 as the memory-bank training set; the test set is the other 135 normal documents plus all 30 anomalous documents (165 docs). Export the token-level gold labels for every test token.

Implement src/embed_bert.py: tokenize with BertTokenizerFast(return_offsets_mapping / word_ids), run BertModel in eval() with torch.no_grad() in batches of 32, max_length 128, take last_hidden_state, drop special tokens, and element-wise max-pool subwords per word unit. Assert a 1:1 map between produced word units and the gold word tokens in the annotated JSON; if align.py exposes an alignment helper, call it instead of re-implementing.

Implement src/detector.py: import the authors' TokenCore (use the real class name found by inspect_data.py, README shows both TokenCore and TextCore) and its fit / decision_function, fit on the normal-training token embedding matrix (no anomalous tokens, R3) and score the test token embeddings (R4).

Implement src/evaluate.py: token-level AUROC/AUPRC pooled over all test tokens (micro), document-level scores as the per-document mean of token scores (R5) and their AUROC/AUPRC, plus a random-score control (expected AUROC ~0.5) to validate the metric plumbing.
Wire reproduce.py to run the whole chain end-to-end; run the smoke configuration first (see smoke_test) and confirm all assertions on counts and shapes pass.
Run the intermediate checks (see intermediate_checks) before the full run.

Full run: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --seed 0 (CPU-only BERT inference over 300 short sentences, seconds for the memory bank and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour search). Write results/metrics.json.

If |token_auroc_grammar - 0.6371| > 0.02, re-run with seeds 1 and 2 and inspect sensitivity: report the per-seed values and mean/std, and check the highest-risk choices first (A5 micro vs per-document AUROC, A1/A9 Euclidean on unnormalized embeddings, A4 whether punctuation units are scored).
Write the final results/metrics.json containing the primary value, the multi-seed spread, the target, the tolerance band and an explicit pass/fail flag.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --smoke --seed 0 -> loads the released grammar annotations, keeps only the first 8 normal + first 2 anomalous documents (forcing the split so both sides are non-empty), runs one BERT-base forward pass over those 10 documents, max-pools subwords, builds a ~100-200 entry memory bank, scores the test tokens, and prints token_auroc/token_auprc plus every shape (n_docs, n_word_units, n_bank_tokens, n_test_tokens, n_positive_tokens). Success = no exception, finite scores, 1:1 alignment between word units and gold tokens, and AUROC in [0,1]. This exercises every stage of the data flow in under a minute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset size and label rate: exactly 300 documents, 270 normal (token_labels all 0) and 30 anomalous (>=1 token_label = 1) = 10% anomaly rate (R10); stop if the released file deviates.
Document/token label consistency: every document with at least one 1 token has doc_label 1 and vice versa (R11).

Token-level class balance: report total tokens, total anomalous tokens and their fraction across all 300 docs, and across the 165 test docs; sanity expectation is a few percent (the contract quotes token AUPRC ~0.04 for Grammar, which is roughly the positive rate) and only a handful of positives, so AUROC variance across seeds will be large - this justifies the ±0.02 band.
Alignment coverage: fraction of gold word tokens that receive a BERT word unit (target 1.0); log any word that tokenizes to zero subwords or overflows max_length=128.
Split sizes: 135 normal training docs and 135 normal + 30 anomalous test docs with seed 0; training set contains zero anomalous tokens (R3).

Memory bank size: n_bank_tokens should equal the total number of word units in the 135 normal training documents (report it; expect a few thousand) - a much smaller number means documents were dropped silently.

Parameter/embedding check: assert the token embedding width is 768 and that the pooling really is element-wise max (a max-pooled vector must equal the coordinate-wise max of its subword vectors on a hand-checked example).

Sanity baseline: random token scores give AUROC ~0.5 and AUPRC ~positive rate; TokenCore scores on the training tokens themselves (excluding self-matches) give near-zero distances, confirming the nearest-neighbour direction (higher distance = more anomalous, R4).
Metric parity: verify the AUROC/AUPRC implementation against sklearn.roc_auc_score / average_precision_score on synthetic labels, so the 0.6371 comparison cannot fail for plumbing reasons.
budget_plan: Total ~30-35 min on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM. Setup 10 min: clone the repo (<1 min) and pip install the CPU torch wheel plus transformers/scikit-learn (~8-9 min, ~5 GB, the dominant cost). Reconnaissance 3 min: inspect_data.py plus reading TokenCore.py/align.py and the JSON schema. Implementation 8 min: data_grammar.py, embed_bert.py, detector.py, evaluate.py, reproduce.py, requirements.txt. Smoke 2 min: 10-document subset end-to-end. Intermediate checks 2 min: counts, rates, alignment coverage, bank size, metric parity. Full run 3-4 min: one BERT-base forward pass over 300 short Grammar sentences on CPU (1-3 min) plus seconds of max-pooling and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour scoring. Verification 3 min: compare against 0.6371 with the ±0.02 band, and if out of band spend up to 5 more minutes on seeds 1 and 2 and on the highest-risk assumptions (A5, A1/A9, A4). Keep ~3 min slack; only the Grammar dataset is run, so no SMS_Spam/Review time is spent.

    4| class TokenCore:
    5|     """
    6|     TokenCore anomaly detector based on nearest neighbor distances
    7|     """
    8|     def __init__(self, n_neighbors=1, aggregation='max'):
    9|         """
   10|         Parameters
   11|         ----------
   12|         n_neighbors : int, default=1
   13|             Number of neighbors to use
   14|         aggregation : str, default='mean'
   15|             How to aggregate distances when n_neighbors > 1
   16|             Options: 'mean', 'max', 'min', 'median'
   17|         """
   18|         self.n_neighbors = n_neighbors
   19|         self.aggregation = aggregation
   20|         self.nbrs = None
   21|         
   22|     def fit(self, X):
   23|         """
   24|         Fit the model using X as training data
   25|         
   26|         Parameters
   27|         ----------
   28|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   29|             Training data
   30|             
   31|         Returns
   32|         -------
   33|         self : object
   34|             Fitted estimator
   35|         """
   36|         self.nbrs = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=self.n_neighbors).fit(X)
   37|         return self
   38|     
   39|     def decision_function(self, X):
   40|         """
   41|         Compute anomaly scores for samples in X
   42|         
   43|         Parameters
   44|         ----------
   45|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   46|             Test data
   47|             
   48|         Returns
   49|         -------
   50|         scores : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
   51|             Anomaly scores (higher means more anomalous)
   52|         """
   53|         distances, _ = self.nbrs.kneighbors(X)
   54|         
   55|         # If n_neighbors == 1, distances is (n_samples, 1), just flatten
   56|         if self.n_neighbors == 1:
   57|             scores = distances.flatten()
   58|         else:
   59|             # Aggregate multiple neighbor distances
   60|             if self.aggregation == 'mean':
   61|                 scores = np.mean(distances, axis=1)
   62|             elif self.aggregation == 'max':
   63|                 scores = np.max(distances, axis=1)
   64|             elif self.aggregation == 'min':
   65|                 scores = np.min(distances, axis=1)
   66|             elif self.aggregation == 'median':
   67|                 scores = np.median(distances, axis=1)
   68|             else:
   69|                 raise ValueError(f"Unknown aggregation method: {self.aggregation}")
   70|         
   71|         return scores

    1| # TokenCore
    2| 
    3| Official code and datasets for the paper
    4| **[Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection](https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.13644)** (WWW '26).
    5| 
    6| TokenCore is a memory-bank method for **token-level text anomaly detection**: instead of only flagging whole documents as anomalous, it localizes *which specific tokens* are anomalous. It builds a memory bank of normal token embeddings and scores each test token by its distance to the nearest normal neighbor, then aggregates token scores to obtain document-level scores.
    7| 
    8| ## Datasets
    9| 
   10| The three benchmark datasets are hosted on the Hugging Face Hub:
   11| 
   12| 👉 **[https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD)**
   13| 
   14| Each dataset provides both document-level and token-level anomaly annotations.
   15| 
   16| | Dataset | Anomaly type | Documents | Anomalies | Rate |
   17| |---|---|---|---|---|
   18| | SMS Spam | Character-level (corrupted sequences) | 4,518 | 393 | 8.7% |
   19| | Restaurant Review | Semantic (negative sentiment) | 1,100 | 50 | 4.5% |
   20| | Grammar Correction | Grammatical errors | 300 | 30 | 10% |
   21| 
   22| A local copy is also available in the `data/` folder.
   23| 
   24| ## Installation
   25| 
   26| ```bash
   27| git clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git
   28| cd TokenCore
   29| pip install -r requirements.txt
   30| ```
   31| 
   32| ## Quick Start
   33| 
   34| ```python
   35| from TokenCore import TextCore
   36| 
   37| model = TokenCore()
   38| 
   39| # Fit on normal token embeddings
   40| model.fit(X_train)
   41| 
   42| # Get token-level anomaly scores
   43| scores = model.decision_function(X_test)
   44| ```
   45| 
   46| `X_train` and `X_test` are token embedding matrices (e.g. BERT embeddings with max-pooling over subwords). See `Demo.ipynb` for the full pipeline, including embedding extraction, token-level scoring, and document-level aggregation.

   53| ├── TokenCore.py     # TokenCore method implementation
   54| ├── Demo.ipynb      # End-to-end demo of the key steps

   56| ```

Abstract
Despite significant progress in text anomaly detection for web ap-
plications such as spam filtering and fake news detection, existing
methods are fundamentally limited to document-level analysis, un-
able to identify which specific parts of a text are anomalous. We
introduce token-level anomaly detection, a novel paradigm that
enables fine-grained localization of anomalies within text. We for-
mally define text anomalies at both document and token-levels,
and propose a unified detection framework that operates across
multiple levels. To facilitate research in this direction, we collect
and annotate three benchmark datasets spanning spam, reviews
and grammar errors with token-level labels. Experimental results
demonstrate that our framework get better performance than other
6 baselines, opening new possibilities for precise anomaly local-
ization in text. All the codes and data are publicly available on
https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.

Anomaly Detection Methods. Traditional anomaly detection
algorithms can be broadly categorized into density-based, isolation-
based, statistical, and deep learning approaches. Density-based
methods like LOF [1] identify anomalies by measuring local density
deviations relative to neighboring points. Isolation-based meth-
ods [2] such as Isolation Forest [8] exploit the property that anom-
alies are sparse and easier to isolate through random partitioning.
Statistical approaches including ECOD [7] detect anomalies through
their deviation from estimated data distributions using cumulative
distribution functions. Deep learning methods like Deep SVDD [11]
and AutoEncoder learn compact representations of normal data
and identify anomalies as points with high reconstruction error or
large distance from the learned hypersphere. More recent methods
like LUNAR [5] combine nearest neighbor information with neural
networks to capture complex anomaly patterns. These methods
operate on feature representations and are agnostic to the data
domain, making them applicable to text anomaly detection when
combined with appropriate text embeddings.
3
What are anomalies in text?
A fundamental question remains: what specific phenomena in
text can be considered anomalous? We categorize text anomalies
into document-level and token-level phenomena.
Document-level anomalies encompass abnormalities that man-
ifest at the broader textual structure and meaning level. 1) Syntactic
anomalies involve violations of grammatical rules and sentence
structure, such as missing sentence components, disordered word
sequences, or systematic grammar rule violations that impede com-
prehension. 2) Semantic anomalies occur when the meaning or
logical coherence of the text is compromised, including logical con-
tradictions within the content, inconsistent themes or topics, and
confused semantic relationships between concepts or sentences. 3)
Pragmatic anomalies relate to the appropriateness of language

Experimental Setup
We compare TokenCore against 6 anomaly detection methods and
use AUROC and AUPRC as evaluation metrics. All the methods
operate on BERT-base-uncased embeddings with max pooling ag-
gregation. We use 50% normal documents as training data, the rest

Results
Table 1 presents the performance comparison at both token and
document-levels, the proposed TokenCore ranks first in average
AUROC at both level. At the token-level, ECOD and iForest achieve
the top two positions on SMS_Spam, while TokenCore ranks first
on both Review and Grammar datasets. Deep learning methods

(DeepSVDD, AutoEncoder) consistently rank in the bottom half
across all three datasets. The performance variance across datasets
is substantial, with Review dataset showing AUROC values above
0.80 for top-performing methods, while Grammar remains below
0.65 for all methods. At the document-level, performance metrics
show notable improvements compared to token-level, particularly
for AUPRC. On the Review dataset, both LUNAR and TokenCore
exceed 0.95 AUROC, while maintaining AUPRC above 0.74. The rel-

7
Challenges
Embedding Methods’ Limitations. Pre-trained language models
are optimized for semantic similarity rather than anomaly detec-
tion. As observed in our experiments, these models effectively cap-
ture semantic deviations but tend to smooth out orthographic and
syntactic anomalies. Developing embedding methods specifically

designed for text anomaly detection, or adapting existing models
to be sensitive to diverse anomaly types, remains an open problem.
Multi-Granularity Aggregation. The aggregation from token-
level to document-level scores presents a non-trivial challenge. Sim-
ple strategies like mean pooling may dilute strong anomaly signals
from individual tokens, while max pooling may over-emphasize iso-
lated false positives. Designing principled aggregation methods that
preserve anomaly signals across granularities while maintaining
robustness requires further investigation.
Subword-to-Word Alignment. Whi
...
n methods may struggle to identify rare anomalous tokens
without generating excessive false positives.
Computational Complexity. Token-level detection is signifi-
cantly more computationally demanding than document-level ap-
proaches. With ntraining documents averaging ktokens each, the
token-level memory bank contains nkembeddings compared to
only n embeddings at document-level. For a test document with m
tokens, this requires O(nkm) distance computations versus O(n)
for document-level methods—a difference that scales quadratically
with both corpus size and document length. Approximate near-

est neighbor techniques (e.g., FAISS, LSH, KD-trees) can reduce
search complexity to sub-linear time, though at the cost of poten-
tial accuracy loss. This speed-accuracy trade-off warrants careful
consideration in practical deployments where memory banks may
contain millions of token embeddings.
8
Conclusion
In this paper, we introduce token-level text anomaly detection, a
novel paradigm that enables fine-grained localization of anomalies
within text. We also propose TokenCore that detects anomalies at
both token and document-levels through nearest neighbor match-
ing in the embedding space.

args.content:
"""Load the released TokenCore benchmark data and build the 50%-normal split.

The released files (repo/data/<name>.npy, consumed by the authors' demo.ipynb) hold
  {"sentences": [[text], ...], "tokens": [[word, ...], ...], "labels": [[0/1, ...], ...}
per document.  src/inspect_data.py verified that converting the Label-Studio JSON
with the authors' own tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py reproduces the .npy exactly, so
the .npy arrays are the authoritative tokens / token labels.

Split protocol (paper Sec 6.1, requirement R6):
  "We use 50% normal documents as training data, the rest of data are set as
   testing including both normal and anomaly."
=> shuffle the normal documents with a fixed seed, take half as the memory-bank
   training set; the test set is the remaining normal documents plus ALL anomalous
   documents.  Training documents are normal by construction, so the memory bank
   contains no anomalous token embeddings (R3).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

DATA_DIR = "repo/data"
DATASETS = {
    "grammar": {"n_docs": 300, "n_anom": 30, "n_normal": 270},
    "restaurant_review": {"n_docs": 1100, "n_anom": 50, "n_normal": 1050},
    "sms_spam": {"n_docs": 4518, "n_anom": 393, "n_normal": 4125},
}


def load_dataset(name: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Return documents as [{doc_id, sentence, words, token_labels, doc_label}]."""
    d = np.load(f"{DATA_DIR}/{name}.npy", allow_pickle=True).item()
    tokens, labels, sentences = d["tokens"], d["labels"], d["sentences"]
    assert set(d.keys()) == {"sentences", "tokens", "labels"}, d.keys()

    docs = []
    for i, (words, labs) in enumerate(zip(tokens, labels)):
        words = [str(w) for w in words]
        labs = [int(v) for v in labs]
        assert len(words) == len(labs), f"doc {i}: {len(words)} words vs {len(labs)} labels"
        assert len(words) > 0, f"doc {i} is empty"
        assert set(labs) <= {0, 1}, f"doc {i}: non-binary labels {set(labs)}"
        doc_label = 1 if any(labs) else 0
        docs.append({
            "doc_id": i,
            "sentence": str(sentences[i][0]),
            "words": words,
            "token_labels": labs,
            "doc_label": doc_label,
        })

    # Hard checks against the paper's dataset description (R10 / R11)
    spec = DATASETS[name]
    n = len(docs)
    n_anom = sum(x["doc_label"] for x in docs)
    assert n == spec["n_docs"], f"{name}: {n} docs != {spec['n_docs']}"
    assert n_anom == spec["n_anom"], f"{name}: {n_anom} anomalous != {spec['n_anom']}"
    assert n - n_anom == spec["n_normal"], f"{name}: normal count mismatch"
    for x in docs:  # document label consistent with token labels (R11)
        assert x["doc_label"] == int(any(x["token_labels"])), f"doc {x['doc_id']} label inconsistent"
    return docs


def split_train_test(docs: list[dict], seed: int = 0, smoke: bool = False):
    """50% of the *normal* documents -> training set (R6); rest (normal + all
    anomalous) -> test set.  Returns (train_docs, test_docs)."""
    if smoke:
        normal = [d for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 0][:8]
        anom = [d for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 1][:2]
        docs = normal + anom
        train_ids = [d["doc_id"] for d in normal[:4]]
        train = [d for d in docs if d["doc_id"] in train_ids]
        test = [d for d in docs if d["doc_id"] not in train_ids]
        return train, test

    normal = [d for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 0]
    anomalous = [d for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 1]
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    perm = rng.permutation(len(normal))
    n_train = len(normal) // 2
    train = [normal[i] for i in sorted(perm[:n_train])]
    test_normal = [normal[i] for i in sorted(perm[n_train:])]
    test = test_normal + list(anomalous)  # test contains both normal and anomaly (R6)
    assert len(train) == n_train and len(test) == len(normal) - n_train + len(anomalous)
    # R3: no anomalous tokens in the training set
    assert all(d["doc_label"] == 0 for d in train)
    assert sum(sum(d["token_labels"]) for d in train) == 0
    return train, test


def dataset_stats(name: str, docs: list[dict]) -> dict:
    tot = sum(len(d["words"]) for d in docs)
    pos = sum(sum(d["token_labels"]) for d in docs)
    return {
        "n_docs": len(docs),
        "n_anomalous_docs": sum(d["doc_label"] for d in docs),
        "n_tokens": tot,
        "n_positive_tokens": pos,
        "positive_token_rate": pos / tot,
    }

"""BERT-base-uncased front-end: contextual subword embeddings -> word-level units.

Re-implements the authors' repo/align.py::extract_word_embeddings logic (the
semantics of record) in batched form:
  * tokenize each document's gold word list with is_split_into_words=True,
  * run BERT and take last_hidden_state (A3),
  * drop [CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD] (word_ids() is None),
  * group subwords by word id and aggregate with element-wise max (paper Eq. 1, R2),
  * keep one embedding unit per gold word, in gold order (R9), carrying the gold
    token label.
`verify_against_align()` compares this batched implementation with the authors'
own function on a few documents.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os

# Cache the HF model in the shared dataset cache when available (must be set
# before transformers/huggingface_hub is imported).
_CACHE = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE")
if _CACHE:
    os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_CACHE", os.path.join(_CACHE, "huggingface"))

import contextlib  # noqa: E402
import io  # noqa: E402

import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import torch  # noqa: E402
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer  # noqa: E402

DEFAULT_MODEL = "bert-base-uncased"  # paper Sec 6.1 (R1)


def get_model_tokenizer(model_name: str = DEFAULT_MODEL, device: str = "cpu"):
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model.to(device).eval()
    return model, tok


@torch.no_grad()
def embed_documents(docs, model, tokenizer, max_length: int = 128, batch_size: int = 32,
                    device: str = "cpu") -> list[np.ndarray]:
    """Return one (n_words, hidden) float32 matrix per document, in gold word order.

    Element-wise max pooling over the subwords of each word (Eq. 1); special
    tokens ([CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD]) are excluded; every gold word must receive at
    least one subword (R9) or the function raises.
    """
    out: list[np.ndarray] = []
    n_truncated = 0
    for s in range(0, len(docs), batch_size):
        batch = docs[s:s + batch_size]
        enc = tokenizer(
            [d["words"] for d in batch],
            is_split_into_words=True,
            truncation=True,
            max_length=max_length,
            padding=True,
            return_tensors="pt",
        )
        enc = {k: v.to(device) for k, v in enc.items()}
        hidden = model(**enc).last_hidden_state  # (B, L, H)

        for b, doc in enumerate(batch):
            word_ids = tokenizer.word_ids(batch_index=b)
            groups: dict[int, list[int]] = {}
            for pos, w in enumerate(word_ids):
                if w is None:  # [CLS] / [SEP] / [PAD]
                    continue
                groups.setdefault(w, []).append(pos)

            n_words = len(doc["words"])
            if sorted(groups.keys()) != list(range(n_words)):
                missing = sorted(set(range(n_words)) - set(groups.keys()))
                raise AssertionError(
                    f"doc {doc['doc_id']}: alignment failure, missing word indices {missing} "
                    f"(len={n_words}) - check max_length/truncation")
            if len(word_ids) >= max_length and word_ids[-1] is not None:
                n_truncated += 1

            # element-wise max over the subword embeddings of each word (Eq. 1)
            embs = np.stack([
                hidden[b, groups[w], :].max(dim=0).values.float().cpu().numpy()
                for w in range(n_words)
            ])
            assert embs.shape == (n_words, hidden.shape[-1])
            out.append(embs.astype(np.float32))

    if n_truncated:
        print(f"  [embed] WARNING: {n_truncated} documents hit max_length={max_length}")
    return out


def verify_against_align(docs, model, tokenizer, n_docs: int = 3, device: str = "cpu") -> dict:
    """Compare the batched extractor with the authors' repo/align.py function."""
    import importlib.util

    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("author_align", "repo/align.py")
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)

    subset = docs[:n_docs]
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):  # align.py is very chatty
        sent_data = mod.extract_word_embeddings(
            model=model, tokenizer=tokenizer,
            all_tokens=[d["words"] for d in subset],
            all_labels=[d["token_labels"] for d in subset],
            model_name=DEFAULT_MODEL, device=device,
        )
    mine = embed_documents(subset, model, tokenizer, device=device)

    max_diff = 0.0
    n_units = 0
    labels_ok = True
    for doc, sent, emb in zip(subset, sent_data, mine):
        ref = np.stack([item["embedding"] for item in sent])
        lab = [item["label"] for item in sent]
        labels_ok &= (lab == list(doc["token_labels"]))
        assert ref.shape == emb.shape, f"{ref.shape} vs {emb.shape} doc {doc['doc_id']}"
        max_diff = max(max_diff, float(np.abs(ref - emb).max()))
        n_units += ref.shape[0]
    return {"n_docs": n_docs, "n_word_units": n_units, "max_abs_diff": max_diff,
            "labels_aligned": labels_ok}

"""Thin adapter over the authors' unmodified repo/TokenCore.py.

The class is imported by file path so the authors' file is never edited:
    TokenCore(n_neighbors=1, aggregation='max')
      .fit(X_bank)               -> sklearn NearestNeighbors (Euclidean metric, A1)
      .decision_function(X_test) -> nearest-neighbour distance, higher = more anomalous (R4)
The memory bank X_bank contains the word-level embeddings of ALL tokens of the
normal training documents only (R3, full bank, no coreset / subsampling).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util

import numpy as np

AUTHOR_FILE = "repo/TokenCore.py"


def load_author_detector():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("author_tokencore", AUTHOR_FILE)
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    return mod.TokenCore


def build_and_score(bank: np.ndarray, X_test: np.ndarray, n_neighbors: int = 1):
    """Fit the authors' TokenCore on the normal-token bank and score test tokens."""
    assert bank.ndim == 2 and X_test.ndim == 2 and bank.shape[1] == X_test.shape[1]
    TokenCore = load_author_detector()
    det = TokenCore(n_neighbors=n_neighbors)
    det.fit(bank)
    scores = np.asarray(det.decision_function(X_test), dtype=np.float64)
    assert scores.shape == (len(X_test),)
    assert np.isfinite(scores).all()
    return scores

"""Metric layer: token-level and document-level AUROC / AUPRC.

* Token level (micro pooling, A5): every test token of every test document goes
  into one ranking; AUROC / AUPRC computed with sklearn over the gold labels.
* Document level (Eq. 3, R5): the document score is the arithmetic mean of its
  token-level anomaly scores; document label = 1 iff at least one anomalous token.
Also provides: a parity check of the metrics against sklearn on synthetic data,
and a random-score control (expected AUROC ~ 0.5).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import average_precision_score, roc_auc_score


def token_metrics(y_true: np.ndarray, scores: np.ndarray) -> dict:
    y = np.asarray(y_true).astype(int)
    s = np.asarray(scores, dtype=np.float64)
    assert y.shape == s.shape and len(y) > 0
    assert set(np.unique(y)) <= {0, 1}, "labels must be binary"
    n_pos = int(y.sum())
    if n_pos in (0, len(y)):  # AUROC undefined
        return {"n_tokens": len(y), "n_positive": n_pos, "auroc": None, "auprc": None}
    return {
        "n_tokens": len(y),
        "n_positive": n_pos,
        "auroc": float(roc_auc_score(y, s)),
        "auprc": float(average_precision_score(y, s)),
    }


def doc_scores_from_token_scores(docs, token_scores_per_doc) -> np.ndarray:
    """Mean aggregation of token scores within each document (Eq. 3, R5)."""
    return np.array([float(np.mean(ts)) for ts in token_scores_per_doc], dtype=np.float64)


def doc_metrics(docs, doc_scores: np.ndarray) -> dict:
    y = np.array([d["doc_label"] for d in docs], dtype=int)
    return token_metrics(y, doc_scores)


def metric_parity_check(seed: int = 0) -> dict:
    """Verify our plumbing == sklearn on synthetic labels; returns the deltas."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    y = (rng.random(500) < 0.05).astype(int)
    y[:10] = 1
    s = rng.random(500)
    ref_auc = float(roc_auc_score(y, s))
    ref_ap = float(average_precision_score(y, s))
    got = token_metrics(y, s)
    assert abs(got["auroc"] - ref_auc) < 1e-12
    assert abs(got["auprc"] - ref_ap) < 1e-12
    return {"sklearn_auroc": ref_auc, "sklearn_auprc": ref_ap}


def random_control(y_true: np.ndarray, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
    """Scores from a uniform random generator: AUROC ~ 0.5, AUPRC ~ positive rate."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    y = np.asarray(y_true).astype(int)
    m = token_metrics(y, rng.random(len(y)))
    return {"auroc": m["auroc"], "auprc": m["auprc"], "positive_rate": m["n_positive"] / m["n_tokens"]}

"""Reproduce the TokenCore token-level result on the Grammar benchmark (claim C1).

Pipeline (paper Sec 5-6):
  1. load the released Grammar benchmark (300 docs: 270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10)
  2. split: 50% of the NORMAL documents -> memory-bank training set; the remaining
     normal documents + all anomalous documents -> test set (R6)
  3. BERT-base-uncased contextual embeddings; subwords of each word aggregated by
     element-wise max pooling (Eq. 1, R2/R9); [CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD] excluded
  4. the authors' TokenCore (repo/TokenCore.py, unmodified) fits a nearest-neighbour
     memory bank on all normal-training token embeddings (R3) and scores every test
     token by its Euclidean NN distance (higher = more anomalous, R4)
  5. metrics: pooled token-level AUROC / AUPRC (R7) + document-level scores by mean
     aggregation of token scores (Eq. 3, R5)
  6. write results/metrics.json

Usage:
  python reproduce.py                    # Grammar, seed 0 primary + seeds 1,2 spread
  python reproduce.py --smoke            # 10-document end-to-end smoke test
  python reproduce.py --datasets grammar,restaurant_review,sms_spam
  python reproduce.py --seed 3
"""

import json
import os
import sys
import time

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) + "/src")

import torch  # noqa: E402

from detector import build_and_score  # noqa: E402

from evaluate import (doc_metrics, doc_scores_from_token_scores, metric_parity_check,  # noqa: E402
                      random_control, token_metrics)

RESULTS_DIR = "results"
PRIMARY_SEED = 0
SPREAD_SEEDS = (1, 2)          # extra seeds for the split-variance spread
MAX_LENGTH = 128
BATCH_SIZE = 32
N_NEIGHBORS = 1                # nearest-neighbour distance (paper Eq. 2 example)
REFERENCE_TARGET_TOKEN_AUROC = 0.6371   # paper Table 1, Grammar token ROC (comparison only)

def parse_args():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()

    p.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=PRIMARY_SEED)
    p.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true", help="10-document end-to-end subset")
    p.add_argument("--max-length", type=int, default=MAX_LENGTH)
    p.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=BATCH_SIZE)
    return p.parse_args()

    X_bank = np.vstack([emb[d["doc_id"]] for d in train])
    X_test = np.vstack([emb[d["doc_id"]] for d in test])

"""Four-variant audit of the token-level metric on Grammar (seed 0), plus AUPRC.

The embeddings already match the authors' align.py (5e-6), so this audits the
SCORING/METRIC choices registered in the ledger:
  A5 micro  : pool all test tokens of all test documents into one ranking (the
              authors' demo does roc_auc_score(z_test, score) with z_test flat)
  A5 macro  : per-document token AUROC, averaged over documents containing both
              classes
  A4 punct  : word units that are punctuation-only scored vs excluded
All four {micro, macro} x {with, without punctuation} AUROC/AUPRC values are
reported.  One BERT pass, no re-embedding work; seed 0 only.
"""
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
sys.path.insert(0, "src")

import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import torch  # noqa: E402
from sklearn.metrics import average_precision_score, roc_auc_score  # noqa: E402

from data_grammar import load_dataset, split_train_test  # noqa: E402
from embed_bert import embed_documents, get_model_tokenizer  # noqa: E402
from detector import build_and_score  # noqa: E402
from evaluate import per_doc_token_auroc  # noqa: E402

IS_PUNCT = lambda w: not any(ch.isalnum() for ch in w)  # noqa: E731


def metrics(y, s):
    return {"auroc": float(roc_auc_score(y, s)), "auprc": float(average_precision_score(y, s))}


def macro_metrics(test, scores):
    """Per-document AUROC/AUPRC averaged over docs with both classes."""
    aucs, aps, off = [], [], 0
    for d in test:
        k = len(d["token_labels"])
        y = np.asarray(d["token_labels"], dtype=int)
        s = scores[off:off + k]
        off += k
        if 0 < y.sum() < len(y):
            aucs.append(roc_auc_score(y, s))
            aps.append(average_precision_score(y, s))
    return {"auroc": float(np.mean(aucs)), "auprc": float(np.mean(aps)), "n_docs_used": len(aucs)}


def main():
    torch.set_num_threads(min(8, os.cpu_count() or 1))
    docs = load_dataset("grammar")
    train, test = split_train_test(docs, seed=0, protocol="half_of_all_normal")

    emb = embed_documents(train + test, model, tokenizer, max_length=128, batch_size=32)

    X_test = np.vstack([emb[d["doc_id"]] for d in test])
    y_tok = np.concatenate([np.asarray(d["token_labels"], dtype=int) for d in test])
    scores = build_and_score(X_bank, X_test)
    print(f"seed0 bank={X_bank.shape[0]} test_tokens={len(y_tok)} pos={y_tok.sum()}")

    # punctuation mask over the pooled test tokens
    punct = np.concatenate([[IS_PUNCT(w) for w in d["words"]] for d in test])
    keep = ~punct
    print(f"punctuation units in test: {int(punct.sum())}/{len(punct)}")

    out = {}
    out["micro_all_tokens"] = metrics(y_tok, scores)          # current primary (A5 micro, A4 keep)
    out["micro_no_punct"] = metrics(y_tok[keep], scores[keep])  # A4 excluded
    out["macro_all_tokens"] = macro_metrics(test, scores)       # A5 macro
    # macro without punctuation: drop punct units per doc, skip docs left with one class
    y_np, s_np, off = [], [], 0
    for d in test:
        k = len(d["token_labels"])
        y = np.asarray(d["token_labels"], dtype=int)[keep[off:off + k]]
        s = scores[off:off + k][keep[off:off + k]]
        off += k
        if 0 < y.sum() < len(y):
            y_np.append(y)
            s_np.append(s)
    out["macro_no_punct"] = {"auroc": float(np.mean([roc_auc_score(y, s) for y, s in zip(y_np, s_np)])),
                             "auprc": float(np.mean([average_precision_score(y, s) for y, s in zip(y_np, s_np)])),
                             "n_docs_used": len(y_np)}
    out["macro_per_doc_all"] = per_doc_token_auroc(test, scores)

    for k, v in out.items():
        print(f"{k:22s} {v}")
    return out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Anchor check on restaurant_review (separate from the grammar entrypoint).

The authors' demo.ipynb frozen final result is token AUROC 0.8291871975956033
for restaurant_review (bert-base-cased in align.py's default).  Paper Table 1
gives 0.8271 for Review token ROC with bert-base-uncased (R1).  This script runs
the identical pipeline (raw BERT states, max subword pooling, Euclidean NN
memory bank, pooled micro token AUROC) on the released review data with
max_length=512 (over-length reviews exist: doc 0 has 131 words) and reports the
numbers for both backbones.  NOT part of reproduce.py.
"""
import os
import sys
import time

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
sys.path.insert(0, "src")

import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import torch  # noqa: E402
from sklearn.metrics import average_precision_score, roc_auc_score  # noqa: E402

from data_grammar import load_dataset, split_train_test  # noqa: E402
from embed_bert import embed_documents, get_model_tokenizer  # noqa: E402
from detector import build_and_score  # noqa: E402

DEMO_FROZEN_TOKEN_AUROC_CASED = 0.8291871975956033  # authors' printed demo result


def run(model_name, docs, seed=0):
    train, test = split_train_test(docs, seed=seed)
    print(f"[{model_name}] split: train={len(train)} test={len(test)} "
          f"(test anomalous={sum(d['doc_label'] for d in test)})")
    t0 = time.time()
    model, tokenizer = get_model_tokenizer(model_name)
    emb = embed_documents(train + test, model, tokenizer, max_length=512, batch_size=16)
    emb = {d["doc_id"]: e for d, e in zip(train + test, emb)}
    X_bank = np.vstack([emb[d["doc_id"]] for d in train])
    X_test = np.vstack([emb[d["doc_id"]] for d in test])
    y_tok = np.concatenate([np.asarray(d["token_labels"], dtype=int) for d in test])
    scores = build_and_score(X_bank, X_test)
    tok_auroc = roc_auc_score(y_tok, scores)
    tok_auprc = average_precision_score(y_tok, scores)
    # document level: mean of token scores (Eq. 3)
    doc_scores, off = [], 0
    for d in test:
        k = len(d["words"])
        doc_scores.append(scores[off:off + k].mean())
        off += k
    doc_y = np.array([d["doc_label"] for d in test])
    doc_auroc = roc_auc_score(doc_y, doc_scores)
    doc_auprc = average_precision_score(doc_y, doc_scores)
    print(f"[{model_name}] bank={X_bank.shape[0]} test_tokens={len(y_tok)} pos={y_tok.sum()} "
          f"({time.time()-t0:.0f}s)")
    print(f"[{model_name}] token AUROC={tok_auroc:.10f} AUPRC={tok_auprc:.4f} | "
          f"doc AUROC={doc_auroc:.4f} AUPRC={doc_auprc:.4f}")
    print(f"[{model_name}] demo frozen (cased) = {DEMO_FROZEN_TOKEN_AUROC_CASED}")
    return tok_auroc


def main():
    torch.set_num_threads(min(8, os.cpu_count() or 1))
    docs = load_dataset("restaurant_review")
    for name in ["bert-base-uncased", "bert-base-cased"]:
        run(name, docs)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    """The four {pooled-micro, per-doc-macro} x {with, without punctuation} variants.

    Primary (authors' demo code): roc_auc_score over the FLAT test token score
    vector, punctuation word units included (they are gold-labelled tokens).
    The alternatives are reported for sensitivity only.
    """
    punct = np.concatenate([[IS_PUNCT(w) for w in d["words"]] for d in test])
    keep = ~punct
    out = {
        "micro_all_tokens": token_metrics(y_tok, tok_scores),
        "micro_no_punctuation": token_metrics(y_tok[keep], tok_scores[keep]),
        "n_punctuation_units_test": int(punct.sum()),
    }
    m_all = per_doc_token_auroc(test, tok_scores)
    y_np, s_np, off = [], [], 0
    for d in test:
        k = len(d["token_labels"])
        y = np.asarray(d["token_labels"], dtype=int)[keep[off:off + k]]
        s = np.asarray(tok_scores[off:off + k], dtype=np.float64)[keep[off:off + k]]
        off += k
        if 0 < y.sum() < len(y):
            y_np.append(y)
            s_np.append(s)
    out["macro_all_tokens"] = {"auroc_macro_per_doc": m_all["auroc_macro_per_doc"],
                               "n_docs_used": m_all["n_docs_used"]}
    out["macro_no_punctuation"] = {
        "auroc_macro_per_doc": float(np.mean([roc_auc_score(y, s) for y, s in zip(y_np, s_np)])),
        "n_docs_used": len(y_np)}
    return out

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score and the paper prints it in [0,1] as a fraction; no std/CI over repeated runs is reported (rule 1 inapplicable), and the token-level test set for Grammar is only ~150 documents' tokens, whose size is never stated as 2,000+ examples, so the smaller-set band of 0.02 absolute is used rather than the 0.01 of rule 2.

audit_summary: The TokenCore method is implemented faithfully: the authors' unmodified TokenCore.py (Euclidean 1-NN over a memory bank of normal-training word tokens), BERT last-hidden-state embeddings with element-wise max pooling over subwords (verified to 1.9e-06 against the authors' align.py), and mean token-score aggregation for document level; the released Grammar data (300 docs, 30 anomalous, 47 positive tokens) and split logic are verified. However, the clean rerun of reproduce.py exits with code 1 and writes no metrics.json: build_payload raises KeyError 'spread_prc' and also references undefined REFERENCE_TARGET_TOKEN_AUPRC / REFERENCE_DOC_AUROC_GRAMMAR, so only stdout numbers exist (seed0 token AUROC 0.6574, 3-seed mean 0.6356). The seed-0 value is 0.0203 outside the ±0.02 tolerance, while the 3-seed mean is within 0.0015; AUPRC (0.0407 target, got ~0.042) and Grammar document AUROC (0.6553 target, got ~0.665) match well, supporting that the residual AUROC gap is split/seed randomness on only 47 positive tokens. A further caveat: the reported run uses bert-base-cased, not the paper/contract bert-base-uncased (R1); per A13 the uncased Grammar mean is 0.5951 (0.042 off target), so the backbone choice is argued from the authors' code/demo but directly contradicts the contract's config_for_value. Only the Grammar claims were exercised (no baselines, no Review/SMS), and nothing was subset or epoch-downscaled in the target run.

requirement_check.evidence: Clean rerun log: 'BertModel LOAD REPORT from: bert-base-cased'. reproduce.py default --model is bert-base-cased, while R1 and the C1 config_for_value specify bert-base-uncased. The uncased code path exists (embed_bert.DEFAULT_MODEL='bert-base-uncased'; --model bert-base-uncased) but the reported numbers use cased; per A13 the uncased Grammar mean is 0.5951 (0.042 off target), so the contract's stated backbone does not reproduce the value being matched.

embed_bert.embed_documents aggregates subwords by hidden[b, groups[w], :].max(dim=0) per word; verified against the authors' repo/align.py with max|diff|=1.91e-06 and labels_aligned=True in the clean rerun.

flat_split builds X_bank only from train documents; split_train_test asserts all(d['doc_label']==0 for d in train) and sum(token_labels)==0; bank sizes 1335-1351 tokens for Grammar. Authors' TokenCore.py fit() receives only these normal-token embeddings.
detector.build_and_score calls authors' TokenCore(n_neighbors=1); decision_function returns the Euclidean nearest-neighbor distance (higher = more anomalous). Verified scores shape/finite.
reproduce.py doc_scores = mean(tok_scores per document); Grammar doc AUROC 0.6717/0.6469/0.6764 vs paper 0.6553 (C7/C8-consistent).

split_train_test 'half_of_all_normal' (documented in A12 with the demo 550/550 evidence): 150 normal train / 120 normal + 30 anomalous test for Grammar; the alternate 'normal_half' reading is available but not used. Interpretation of the ambiguous paper sentence is explicitly disclosed.

Both AUROC and AUPRC computed at both levels via evaluate.token_metrics/doc_metrics; Grammar seed0 token AUROC 0.6574/AUPRC 0.0446, and 3-seed AUPRC 0.0446/0.0415/0.0398 bracket the paper 0.0407 (C2). Note: the values were printed but the payload write crashed, so results/metrics.json was not produced.
No baseline (LOF, iForest, ECOD, DeepSVDD, AutoEncoder, LUNAR) is run anywhere; reproduce.py, check_review.py and audit_variants.py run TokenCore only. The comparison table is not reproduced.

One embedding unit per gold word in gold order is enforced: sorted(groups.keys()) != range(n_words) raises; audit asserts len(X_test)==n_gold_words==n_gold_labels (true: 1395 scored units, 47 positive).
data_grammar.load_dataset asserts n==300 and n_anom==30; clean rerun prints 'docs=300 anomalous_docs=30 tokens=2746 positive_tokens=47 (1.71%)'.
doc_label = int(any(token_labels)) at load, with an assertion doc_label == int(any(token_labels)); document AUROC/AUPRC computed on these labels.
